title: runtime: add optional kernel-selection debug dump tagged to perf runs
author: Yuki Sato
release_notes: Adds an opt-in kernel-selection debug dump for benchmark/perf runs. Disabled by default; when enabled, emits structured JSONL records describing selected kernel + fallback reasons, tagged with run_id for regression attribution.
description:
Context: For the Q1 2026 perf baseline & representative workload suite we need to attribute regressions to kernel auto-selection changes (vs scheduler/queueing vs environment). Today, kernel selection decisions are not externally visible, and it has been hard to explain why the runtime picked a different kernel between two runs with “identical” workloads.

This PR adds an opt-in “kernel selection debug dump” that records the kernel selection decision at the point of selection, tagged to perf run metadata (run_id, workload_id) so the benchmark harness can collect and store it alongside the manifest + results.

What’s included: (1) A new runtime config gate: kernel_selection.debug_dump.enabled (default false). (2) A sink that writes JSONL to a local file (or stdout in container mode) with a bounded rate + sampling controls. (3) A stable record schema capturing model family, sequence-length regime, selected kernel ID, candidate set, and explicit fallback reasons when applicable. (4) Plumbs run_id/workload_id from the perf harness via existing request metadata header (x-redwood-perf-run-id) and stores it in the dump record (no prompts / no token content).

Output format (one JSON object per line, JSONL): {"ts":"2026-01-14T22:41:13.512Z","run_id":"rb-2026q1-llama3-70b-us-east-h100-00042","workload_id":"chat_streaming_v1","model":"llama3.1-70b-instruct","gpu":"H100-SXM","sm":"90","dtype":"fp16","seq_regime":"prefill_0_1k_decode_0_256","selected_kernel":"flashattn_v2","kernel_variant":"fa2_causal_packkv","candidates":["flashattn_v2","triton_sdpa"],"fallback":false,"fallback_reason":"","constraints":{"cuda":"12.4","driver":"550.54","triton":"2.2"},"notes":""}.

Enablement: Intended for benchmarks/perf canary only. Set REDWOOD_KERNELSEL_DUMP=1 or config kernel_selection.debug_dump.enabled=true in the perf job environment; optionally set kernel_selection.debug_dump.sample_rate (default 0.01) and kernel_selection.debug_dump.max_records_per_minute (default 600). A file path can be specified with kernel_selection.debug_dump.path; default is /var/log/redwood/kernel_selection_dump.jsonl (falls back to /tmp if unwritable).

Safety/perf considerations: Dump is disabled by default. When enabled, writes are async (single background thread + bounded queue). If queue fills, we increment a counter and drop records rather than blocking request processing. Record content is strictly non-sensitive (no prompts, no user IDs). Added a unit test to assert prompt text never enters the dump record.

Docs: Adds a short section to docs/perf/debugging.md describing how to enable the dump and attach it to benchmark artifacts.

Follow-ups: Once perf-canary is wired, we should add a panel in baseline dashboards that links run_id -> kernel dump artifact and add an automated diff tool for “kernel decision delta” between two runs (tracked separately).

review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka (review): Can we guarantee the dump doesn’t add p99 overhead when enabled? Also want explicit fallback reason codes vs free-form strings.

Yuki Sato (author): Added async writer with bounded queue + drop-on-full behavior; request path just enqueues a small struct. Also replaced free-form fallback_reason with an enum->string mapping (e.g., "constraint_driver_version", "seq_len_out_of_range", "disabled_by_flag", "oom_risk_guard").

Grace Kim (review): Please include the candidate kernel list only when sample_rate triggers; otherwise record size is big. Also ensure kernel_variant is stable across refactors (avoid debug-only names).

Yuki Sato (author): Done: candidates only included when kernel_selection.debug_dump.include_candidates=true (default false). kernel_variant now uses the existing KernelId::stable_name() used in logs, not the internal class name.
Marcus Reed (review): The run_id header name should be consistent with the benchmark harness. We already use x-redwood-bench-run-id in benchmark-lab. Can you support both for now?
Yuki Sato (author): Added support for both headers with x-redwood-perf-run-id taking precedence. Also logs a warning once per process if both are set but differ.
Rina Kobayashi (review): Need a clear artifact path for the harness to collect. Please default to /tmp in containers; /var/log is not always mounted.
Yuki Sato (author): Updated default path resolution: try /var/log/redwood, then /tmp/redwood. Also added a startup log line: "kernel selection dump enabled: path=..." for harness discovery.
Allison Grant (review): Please add metrics for dump health and make sure labels don’t explode cardinality (run_id is high-cardinality).

Yuki Sato (author): Added counters without run_id label: kernel_selection_debug_dump_records_total, kernel_selection_debug_dump_dropped_total, kernel_selection_debug_dump_write_failures_total. run_id only appears in the dump file, not metrics.
Hiro Tanaka (approval): LGTM after the enum reason codes change. Thanks for keeping it opt-in and low overhead.
Marcus Reed (approval): LGTM; header compatibility appreciated.
Rina Kobayashi (approval): LGTM. We’ll wire artifact collection in benchmark-lab.
